LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD passes the narrow safety gate for `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

The `source` array contains a single entry: `git+https://invent.kde.org/multimedia/amarok.git`. This is the project's own upstream source on KDE's official Invent server (KDE's GitLab instance), which is the expected and appropriate location for the amarok-git package. The corresponding `sha512sums=('SKIP')` is the required standard practice for VCS sources.

The `pkgver()` function performs a standard `git describe` followed by a `sed` transformation to format the version string — there is no network access, no code execution beyond standard git/sed, and no exfiltration.

The top-level scope contains only variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, dependencies, etc.) with no command substitution or execution.

The `build()` and `package()` functions contain standard `cmake` build commands, but these will not execute during this gate (`--nobuild --noprepare`), so they are out of scope here.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard git+https source from KDE upstream; safe to fetch and source.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD for `amarok-git` is a standard packaging recipe with no security concerns. The source is pulled directly from the official KDE GitLab repository (`git+https://invent.kde.org/multimedia/amarok.git`), which is the expected upstream for this KDE multimedia application. The `sha512sums=('SKIP')` entry is normal and required for VCS (git) sources.

The `pkgver()` function uses a standard `git describe` with `sed` substitution to generate the version string — typical for -git packages. The `build()` function invokes `cmake` with reasonable options (disabling iPod/gPodder support and tests), and `package()` uses the standard `DESTDIR` cmake install pattern. Dependencies are a sensible set of Qt6, KDE Frameworks, and media-handling libraries consistent with Amarok's purpose as a KDE music player.

No suspicious network requests, obfuscation, unexpected file operations, or dangerous commands are present. The package follows ordinary AUR packaging practices throughout.
</details>
